text: River | Official Trailer
context:
RIVER "will drown you in pure terror." (TheWrap) Only in theaters January 15

The sun is down. The boat is dead. There’s no cell service. And there’s someone standing, staring, from the shore. From the producers of Backrooms and Obsession comes a vivid, visceral new vision in the slasher genre, marking an electrifying feature-film debut by writer-director Joshua Giuliano. 

River stars Jane Levy (Don’t Breathe, Evil Dead), Jessica Rothe (Happy Death Day films, Pulse) and Max Mattern (Cape Fear, Devil in Disguise: John Wayne Gacy) as estranged siblings who reunite in their rural hometown after the death of their father. As they set out to scatter his ashes at his favorite spot on a remote river, the trip devolves into a fight for survival as they are mercilessly hunted by a disturbing masked figure played by Dane DiLiegro (Prey, Only Murders in the Building).

Acquired by Universal Pictures and Blumhouse Atomic Monster following a rapturous screening at Midnight Madness at the Toronto International Film Festival, River is produced by Steven Schneider (executive producer Insidious franchise, Split) via his company Spooky Pictures, and Nick Antosca (creator Cape Fear series, Verity) and Alex Hedlund (executive producer Cape Fear series, Verity) via their company Eat The Cat. 

The film’s executive producers are Jeffrey Tinnell, Robert Tinnell, Matt Brodlie, Jonathan Kier, Ben Ross and Jason Blum. Universal Pictures, Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Independent Film Company present a Shudder Original Production, in association with Upgrade.

author: Alfredo Federico Robelo
text: 15 Actors That Were Older Than You Thought They Were
context:
Good child actors are hard to come by, and when you find the ideal performer, in just a few years they’ll stop being a child. For roles about teenagers, however, finding ideal candidates is far easier, since a lot of adults can play them convincingly. 
 So convincingly, in fact, that audiences might not realize the actors were adults at all. Of course, there are films where the entire high school is populated by adults, but in well made productions, we can suspend our disbelief. These are the actors that, when their movies happened, seemed eternally young.

author: Alfredo Federico Robelo
text: 15 Actors Who Allegedly Didn’t Get Along On Set
context:
Hollywood loves selling the illusion of perfect chemistry, even if behind the scenes, plenty of famous co-stars reportedly could barely stand each other. Sometimes it was personality clashes, creative disagreements, or simply spending too many exhausting months trapped together during difficult productions. In other cases, the tension became so obvious that audiences eventually noticed it onscreen. 
 Legendary old-school feuds and modern blockbuster drama make up these conflicts, which became part of entertainment history almost as much as the movies and shows themselves. Some rivalries cooled off with time, while others stayed bitter for decades. Either way, these productions prove that great performances do not always come from friendly working relationships. 
 The post  15 Actors Who Allegedly Didn’t Get Along On Set  appeared first on  Den of Geek .

author: Leandro Beroldo
text: 10 TV Shows That Were Way Too Complicated to Ever Finish Properly
context:
Some television shows build massive worlds, layered mysteries, and sprawling character arcs that feel exciting while they are unfolding, but far harder to resolve satisfyingly. As the story expands, more plot threads, timelines, and unanswered questions accumulate, eventually creating pressure that even the strongest writing teams struggle to resolve cleanly. In many cases, the ambition that made the show great in the first place becomes the same reason the ending feels rushed, confusing, or incomplete. Audiences are left with lingering questions because nothing was explained, but because too much was built to be tied together neatly. These are the kinds of series where the journey often outshines the destination. 
 The post  10 TV Shows That Were Way Too Complicated to Ever Finish Properly  appeared first on  Den of Geek .

author: Leandro Beroldo
text: Actors Who Hit the Jackpot and Then Pretty Much Dipped
context:
Most actors spend their entire careers chasing one massive hit that can change their lives forever. Some become lifelong Hollywood fixtures afterward, while others surprisingly step away once they achieve huge success. In a few cases, actors earned enormous fame, money, or cultural recognition from a single movie or franchise before deciding they had little interest in staying constantly active in the industry. Some focused on family life, others pursued completely different careers, and a few simply preferred privacy over nonstop celebrity attention. Their careers never fully disappeared, though compared to the level of fame they once reached, their output became surprisingly small. These actors essentially hit the jackpot and quietly moved on.

author: Alfredo Federico Robelo
text: 14 Actors Who Chose Quality Over Quantity
context:
Actors, like any other person, need to work to pay the bills. Sure, a lot of them have a lot more money than the average person, but that isn’t true for all performers, much less at the start of their careers. And yet, there are a few actors that, once they gained some renown, decided to be more picky on the films they starred in. 
 Not all of the films they chose were instant classics, but that’s not why they chose them. These are actors clearly working their craft to the best of their ability, searching for roles that challenge them. They may not have starred in plenty of films, but the filmography they are in was worth it.

author: Alfredo Federico Robelo
text: Movies Everyone Quotes Without Having Actually Seen Them
context:
Movies become instant classics by covering deep themes, being incredibly entertaining, or having quotable lines. That last batch of movies have a tendency of becoming memes, catchphrases and joke enders, to the point that the quote is far more memorable than the film itself. 
 This has the unfortunate effect of audiences quoting movies they’ve never seen, with the phrases exploding in popularity through other media. There are people that don’t even know the quote is from a movie, since the quote has morphed so much. We hope that this article makes you watch the movies with the immortal quotes.

text: 14 Actors Who’ve Been in Everything, But You Might Not Recognize
context:
Depending on the decade, the entertainment industry tends to use the same actors across plenty of films, mainly due to their popularity. This is something we’re used to, but the characters behind the big leads also get reused often, something we tend to overlook since, well, they’re in the background. 
 Still, their performances have merit, since someone needs to play all those roles. Once you see them, though, you can’t unsee them, so be prepared to recognize them everywhere. It’s incredible how prolific these actors are, leaving a legacy of their own by being in so many memorable movies. 
 The post  14 Actors Who’ve Been in Everything, But You Might Not Recognize  appeared first on  Den of Geek .

author: Alfredo Federico Robelo
text: 15 Movies We Don’t Believe Anyone Actually Watched All the Way Through
context:
Watching movies is meant to be a joyful experience, even if you’re watching a tense thriller. The point is to have a good time, hence why films are part of the entertainment business. But what happens when a movie isn’t something enjoyable, but something you have to endure? 
 This is the topic for today: movies that are so hard to get through, people have walked out of cinemas out of sheer frustration. And not because they’re controversial; they’re just plain bad. If you’re planning a movie night, these are the movies to avoid. Or, if you’re brave, these are the movies to endure. 
 The post  15 Movies We Don’t Believe Anyone Actually Watched All the Way Through  appeared first on  Den of Geek .

author: Fernanda Arnaud
text: 15 People Share the Weirdest Jobs Someone They Know Works
context:
Most people know someone who works in an office, teaches kids, or spends their days dealing with customers. Then there are the people whose jobs require a much longer explanation. Someone has to make wigs for opera singers, jump out of planes to fight wildfires, and create fake injuries for medical training. Those jobs might sound like something a writer made up, but they're perfectly real professions. When Reddit users started sharing the strangest careers held by people they know, the answers covered everything from entertainment to science and some surprisingly specific hobbies. Here are 15 unusual jobs that might make your own nine-to-five sound pretty normal. 
 The post  15 People Share the Weirdest Jobs Someone They Know Works  appeared first on  Den of Geek .

author: Alfredo Federico Robelo
text: The 14 Worst Horror Movie Franchises That Refuse To Die
context:
More often than not, what makes a horror movie work is the novelty of the premise. Well, franchises don’t work on novelty, they work by cashing in on known tropes, nostalgia, and an established IP. That doesn’t mean that the movies made for the franchises are guaranteed to be bad, it just means they’re very likely to be bad. 
 This list is a memorial to those great ideas that were run into the ground by endless, often terrible, follow-up films. After all, once the franchise moves to space, you know that something has been broken along the way.

               Dr. Lioba Schlösser (*1988) ist Filmwissenschaftlerin. Sie promovierte 2022 zum Thema »Perspektiven filmischer Überwindung der bipolaren Geschlechternorm durch Rekurse auf mythisches Potenzial« an der JGU Mainz und vertritt seit Anfang 2025 die Professur »Theorie der Wahrnehmung, Kommunikation und Medien« an der Münster School of Design der FH Münster. Außerdem arbeitet sie als Koordinatorin für Gleichstellung und Diversity an der Heinrich-Heine-Universität Düsseldorf und unterrichtet als Dozentin an der Filmakademie Ludwigsburg.
